ORAL JUDGMENT:
1.

This appeal preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assails the judgment and order dated 11.04.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Yavatmal (hereinafter referred to as "Tribunal" for short) in M.A.C.P. No.73/2005 on the ground that the Tribunal has not assessed the income of the deceased properly while granting compensation to the appellants/claimants on account of loss of dependency due to the death of Faruk Ali who died in vehicular accident on 02.06.2004.

2. Deceased Faruk, who was the owner and driver of the truck bearing registration No.MH296883,
was engaged in the business of transportation.
On the fateful day, the deceased parked his vehicle on the extreme side of the road and kept the parking light on.
The deceased alighted from the truck for tightening the 3 fa679.14.odt rope of the truck alongwith one Bahadur Ali and went to the back side of the truck.
At that time, the offending truck bearing registration No.AP26T9297, which was insured with respondent no.3-Insurer gave a dash to the said stationed truck from the back side.
In the said collision, Faruk and the conductor/coolie Bahadur Ali were crushed and died on the spot.
An offence came to be registered under Sections 279 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code against the offending vehicle.

The appellants being wife and children of deceased Faruk Ali filed a claim petition before the Tribunal and consequently, the Tribunal granted the compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- apart from loss of estate and consortium by assessing the income of the deceased @
Rs.3,500/- per month.

3. The finding of Tribunal assessing income of the deceased Faruk Ali @Rs.3,500/- per month has been challenged in the present appeal apart from entitlement to future prospects and enhancement of loss of estate and consortium.
4. Mr. Narwade, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that deceased was not only the driver but also the owner of the truck and was engaged in the business of transportation.

The fact that the deceased was paying a monthly 4 fa679.14.odt instalment of Rs.8,500/- itself goes to suggest that the deceased was earning @Rs.20,000/- per month and the amount of Rs.8,500/- cannot be termed as expense being repayment of loan.
Therefore, the Tribunal has committed a serious error while assessing the income of the deceased and granted the compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- only.

sentences.text: 5. Conversely, Ms Anita Mategonkar, learned counsel for respondent no.3 vehemently submitted that the amount of Rs.8,500/- includes the interest which is to be treated as an expense and is to be deducted from the income.
According to her, learned Tribunal after considering the facts on record has properly assessed the income at Rs.3,500/- per month.
However, she submitted that so far as other benefits are concerned, an appropriate order may be passed.

6. Having heard learned counsels for the respective parties and having gone through the material available on record, 1 2017 (16) SCC 680 5 fa679.14.odt it transpires that the accident occurred due to the fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Perusal of the record goes to show that the appellants have proved that deceased Faruk Ali was paying a monthly instalment of Rs.8,500/-
towards repayment of loan which was taken for purchasing the truck.

It is to be noted that when deceased was paying monthly instalment of Rs.8,500/- per monthly then obviously, he would have been earning more than what has been assessed by the Tribunal particularly, when deceased Faruk Ali who was an owner and was driving the truck himself for saving the salary that could be given to a driver.

No doubt the amount of Rs.8,500/- may include interest which may be treated as an expense but it also include the principal amount towards purchase of capital goods which cannot be treated as an expense.
Be that as it may, the fact remains that deceased Faruk Ali was the driver and owner of the truck and he himself was driving the vehicle.
Hence, in all probability he might be earning not less than Rs.7,000/- per month.

Therefore, his annual salary would be around Rs.84,000/-
7.
This takes me to question of awarding future prospects and proper consortium.

It is worthwhile to mention here the decision in the case of Magma General Insurance Company 6 fa679.14.odt Limited vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors. 1, wherein the Supreme Court has held that parents are also entitled for Filial consortium at rate of Rs.40,000/- apart from the compensation towards funeral expenses and loss of estate at the rate of Rs.15,000/- each.
